title: Internal: Filing a Debit Card Transaction Dispute
summary: This document instructs agents on filing a debit card transaction dispute under Regulation E, including customer liability based on discovery timing ($50 if within 2 business days, $500 within 60 days, unlimited after 60 days/no recovery). It covers required pre-filing checks, dispute category rules (including fraud vs non-fraud), earliest transaction selection for duplicates, open-dispute limits by checking tier (Entry 2, Mid 3, Premium 4, Elite 5), ATM process branching, and the tool file_debit_card_transaction_dispute_6281 parameters and card_action mapping (e.g., card_present_fraud/card_not_present_fraud → close_and_reissue).
faqs: What is my maximum liability if I report an unauthorized debit card transaction within 2 business days, within 60 days, or after 60 days?
What information and eligibility requirements must an agent collect before filing a debit card transaction dispute?
How should an agent choose the disputed transaction when there are duplicate charges—should they dispute the earliest one?
How do I classify a dispute: unauthorized transaction vs card-present fraud vs card-not-present fraud?
What are the open-dispute limits by checking account tier (Entry/Mid/Premium/Elite) when filing disputes?
For fraud-related disputes over $500, do we need a police report, and how does the written statement affect provisional credit? (Uses provisional_credit_eligible.)
